gddGap: The GDD sets no level count, tiers or level list. This is an extra proposed level (order 6, after the five in levels.json) that introduces the GDD-named Rust units in escalation: Iron Line cordon, then Watchers, then Breakers. Wave numbers and the 150 s limit are placeholders in the Tier 0 shape. Uses the proposed expansion enemies from rust-gdd-units.json, so it depends on owner approval of those.
name: The Iron Line Push
theme: Stewpot Gardens, where the Rust have strung a line of barriers between the planters and the food stalls; steam still rises from the stew pots behind it.
intro: The Iron Line is holding the garden gate. Faceless helmets, cheap plating. Zed's neighbours are watching from the stalls. Push the line back, then the Watchers and Breakers behind it.
outro: The line gives way and the stew pots are steaming again. A neighbour waves a ladle from the stall. The garden is the neighbourhood's once more.
notes: Bosses per the-story-campaign#1 (miniBoss/mainBoss are enemy ids, not wave entries). Holt arena flavour: lab with gas vents (old "Undercity", flavour only). Owner decision: the mini-boss arrives as a mini wave, a beatable pressure wave led by the mini-boss, deliberately not too hard and not a hard gate. Owner decision: the main boss gets its own separate fight phase after the waves (own arena phase, phases per the GDD).

miniBoss.note: beatable pressure wave led by the mini-boss

gddGap: The GDD says Copper Fangs serve boss-tier encounters but gives no level list, tiers or boss placement. This proposes a mini-boss level (order 7): a ladder of single units rising Watcher, Breaker, Copper Fang. Each wave has count 1 because the validator requires wave counts not to shrink, so a lone boss wave must follow count-1 waves; mixed-escort boss waves need a schema extension (one enemy per wave today).
name: Copper Fang at the Courts
theme: The forest-green basketball courts, hoops bent but standing, with a Rust command post set up at centre court and kids' chalk drawings still on the asphalt.
intro: Varr's favourite is guarding centre court: a Copper Fang with a shield and a hook. Block, dodge, parry. Give the kids their court back.
outro: The shield cracks and the Fang is pushed back off the court. Somewhere a ball bounces, then another. Zed breathes out. Game on.
notes: Bosses per the-story-campaign#1 (miniBoss/mainBoss are enemy ids, not wave entries). Campaign main boss is "Elite Rust Gauntlet", which has no enemy item: open question, not invented. Old "Rust Military Compound" title is flavour only. Owner decision: the mini-boss arrives as a mini wave, a beatable pressure wave led by the mini-boss, deliberately not too hard and not a hard gate. No boss phase on this level. Main boss 'Elite Rust Gauntlet' to be defined by the owner in the GDD; not invented here.

miniBoss.note: beatable pressure wave led by the mini-boss

gddGap: The GDD gives Overseer Halden Varr, "The Architect of Rust" (GDD wording, owner-confirmed) the Main Boss slot in the Corporate Tower command chamber, but defines no level list or tiers. This proposes the end-level boss encounter (order 8) as the last level of the Rust push, against Varr. Varr's own summons (Command Override, Drone Command) are behaviour in rust-gdd-units.json, not wave data, so waves here are a single-unit ladder (counts cannot shrink; one enemy type per wave). The district id is the closest existing lore district (Songwindow Heights, surveillance tower and screens); the Corporate Tower arena itself is not yet a district, a GDD gap. The named Overseers Kade Voss (Neon Market) and Rhea Calder (Factory floor) have no level yet.
name: The Overseer's Tower
theme: Songwindow Heights, where a surveillance tower and propaganda screens loom over the windows that used to play music; murals half-painted over in grey.
intro: Varr runs the whole city from this tower, with squads, drones and shields at his call. Fight through, reach the command chamber and break the order. Let the music back in.
outro: The screens flicker out and Varr gives up the tower. A window opens, then another, and music drifts down over the Heights. The first mural stroke goes back up.
notes: Bosses per the-story-campaign#1 (miniBoss/mainBoss are enemy ids, not wave entries). Varr arena flavour: command chamber (old "Corporate Tower", flavour only). Owner decision: the mini-boss arrives as a mini wave, a beatable pressure wave led by the mini-boss, deliberately not too hard and not a hard gate. Owner decision: the main boss gets its own separate fight phase after the waves (own arena phase, phases per the GDD).
